findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so no default server-side encryption (particularly KMS) is enforced for the reports bucket, which receives the vendor roster object.
No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so the bucket relies entirely on account defaults and could be exposed by a subsequent ACL or bucket policy change.
No logging block routes access events to the audit_trail bucket, so reads and writes of the stored vendor data are not recorded for detection or forensics.
The ledger export bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial ledger data is stored without an enforced server-side encryption default.
No logging block is configured, so access to sensitive financial exports is not audited to the audit_trail bucket.
Despite the private ACL, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guardrail prevents a future ACL or bucket policy change from exposing ledger data publicly.
The model artifacts bucket enables versioning and logging but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored artifacts without enforced default encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block restricts public ACLs or policies on this bucket, leaving proprietary model artifacts exposed to accidental public sharing.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational runbooks (which commonly contain internal infrastructure detail) are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is defined, so access to operational runbooks is not recorded in the audit_trail bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so account-level or future policy changes could make internal runbooks publicly readable.

The central audit log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and its log-delivery-write ACL grants the S3 log delivery group write access; without the guardrail a policy or ACL change could expose audit logs revealing access patterns and object names.

The audit log destination has no object lock / WAL protection and force_destroy = true permits Terraform to delete the bucket and every retained log object, undermining the integrity of the audit trail that the other buckets depend on.

The vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that has no default encryption, so this third-party data is stored without encryption controls.

The reports bucket is named "<env>-reports" while model_artifacts uses "<env>-reports-science"; combined with no public access block or encryption on reports_archive, a policy written against the "<env>-reports" prefix pattern can unintentionally grant access to the model_artifacts bucket as well.
